key_evidence: On 11 September 2026 the High Court sentenced Chow Hang-tung to 7 years 3 months, Lee Cheuk-yan to 7 years and Albert Ho to 5 years 2 months for inciting subversion under the National Security Law, and fined the Hong Kong Alliance HK$1.5 million. The judges noted the case did not involve violence or the threat of violence.
The UN Human Rights Office (tier 4) called it another regrettable outcome of the deeply flawed National Security Law; High Commissioner Volker Türk called for the sentences to be quashed.
On 12 September the HKSAR Government (tier 5, primary conduct) rejected the criticism as smears and said the verdicts were reached free from any interference or political consideration.

The 2026-07-31 assessment (29.4) carried a downward watch flag for further escalation within four months. The sentencing lands six weeks later, the third escalation in the pattern after bookstore raids and prosecutions of people with intellectual disability.
ATTRIBUTION: prosecution, police characterisation, sentencing and the government's defence are all HKSAR institutions, so they are scored against this global-cities entity.

evidence.quote: In the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, today's imposition of lengthy jail terms on three activists and a heavy fine on the affiliated civil society organisation is another regrettable outcome of the deeply flawed National Security Law.
evidence.claim: The UN Human Rights Office characterised the sentences as a regrettable outcome of a deeply flawed law; it supports the I1 and E4 moves.
evidence.source: UN Human Rights Office (OHCHR), spokesperson Seif Magango (via Scoop)

evidence.quote: Leadership by the Communist Party of China is the core of the fundamental system established by the Constitution; acts to overthrow or undermine that leadership fall within the scope of offences referenced in the Hong Kong National Security Law.

evidence.claim: HRW characterised the 21 August conviction as criminalising public mourning (pre-window context for the watch-flag pattern).

notes: Filed under the magnitude trigger (-5.9). No band change: 26.9 stays in Developing. About -3.4 of the delta was already measured on 2026-07-31, and about -2.5 comes from four in-window integer moves (E4, AB1, S4, I1). Every movement rests on HKSAR conduct, not calibration. Confidence is medium, not high: the delta is only 0.9 above the trigger, and the full sentencing reasons were not fetched. The published 32.8 has never been changed. Proposed subdimensions cover all 8 dimensions because every dimension differs from the published vector (the published values are placeholder-granular, for example AWR 2.5 against a measured 2.2).
